key_terms: A producer setting under which the partition leader acknowledges a write after the in-sync replica requirement is met. On a one-broker topic it adds no redundancy.
The replicas currently caught up with the partition leader. min.insync.replicas sets how many must acknowledge an acks=all write.
A producer that uses a producer identifier and sequence numbers so brokers can suppress duplicates from its own supported retries. It does not deduplicate separate send calls.
A send whose acknowledgement was lost, leaving the producer unable to know whether the record was appended.
The bounded time a producer allows for a send, including retries, before reporting failure.

worked_examples.title: Configure an idempotent transactional producer
worked_examples.interpretation: These lines come from the streaming project TransactionProbe.java. Idempotence lets the broker drop a resend of the same producer sequence number, and acks set to all makes the acknowledgement wait for the in-sync replicas, which is one replica in this single-broker workshop. The delivery timeout bounds how long a send can retry before its future fails. None of these settings recognizes two separate send calls with the same business key as duplicates.

worked_examples.title: Read committed and uncommitted views of the topic
worked_examples.code:
cd work/streaming
bash run.sh start
bash run.sh check-transactions
worked_examples.interpretation: In an owned workshop, the check prints a JSON line with committed_records 3, uncommitted_records 4 and aborted_hidden true. The read_committed consumer sees order-1 plus two identical same-business-id records, while read_uncommitted also sees the aborted order-2 value. The two identical records are correct Kafka behavior: they came from two awaited send calls, so deduplicating them is the consumer's business rule, not a broker guarantee.
